Wade: Sure, most Wades are builders until they realise they have a lot more fun staying at home and seeing how much pain they can inflict upon themselves by squashing their own hand in a vice. If that's the case then this Wade might even baits dogs for a hobby. However, a mutated set of Wade genes often produces the funniest man in, not just the room, but the whole damn building. I hope you're dealing with the latter. Management.
Wah: Wah will have a crack at anything, and he’ll do it with good intention. For instance, the first time he took acid he ended up out on the street in broad daylight and when he began to feel as though his clothes were made of bugs he stripped naked and wound up totally lost. He climbed up a tree to try and escape the bugs on the ground, until he spotted an old man whom he hoped might tell him where he was. Wah jumped down, all smiles, until the old fellow began belting his naked buttocks with his walking stick. Writhing on the ground in agony and pleading for mercy, Wah was actually delighted when the cops showed up because the paddy wagon they put him in felt like a giant, cool living room, plus no one was beating him. They didn’t even charge him.
Wal: Wal likes his meat and three veg for dinner followed by a bowl of ice-cream. He volunteers for the emergency services.
Waldemar: Like Merlin the Magician, Waldemar is the textbook eccentric genius.
Waleed: Waleed is well-oiled, be it philosophically, spiritually, socially and financially. He might even be a little too well-oiled.
Wally: As the genial head of the local APEX or Rotary branch, Wally is filled with the deeds of goodness that are misguided only 10% of the time.
Walter: Abused by his wife, Walter speaks very slowly and after orgasm, which is a rare event in itself, he often can’t speak for days.
Ward: In a past life Ward was an SS officer in the Third Reich, so he's got a bit to catch up on when it comes to unconditional love. He's making progress though…
Warne:
“Hello, I’m Warne,” he says, quietly. 
Immediately everyone is looking for a punchline, but it doesn’t come. Warne is a calm, unassuming and purposeful man and there it is.
Warny: See Kylie, although he is way less dignified.
Warren: As a variety of ferret, Warren is industrious and crafty. After some initial weirdness, he is usually quite loveable but if you corner him or freak him out too much, he’s liable to start smelling odd and he might have a go at you. Not the most nostalgic of creatures.
Warrick: A muscle bound twit who specializes in verbal diarrhoea and offending women
Warwick: Highly educated (he finished primary school) Warwick still has trouble doing up his shoe laces so they stay done up. Why is that Warwick? We hope that it's not used as a ploy to stare up girls' skirts Warwick. It's not, is it? (Would we credit it? Sadly, yes we would.)
Watto: Watto' hates eating at restaurants because it means he has to use a knife and fork. He's much happier with a meat pie and no shoes.
Waylon:
Waylon, you do understand of course that you and you alone construct your reality? So, for a friendly and relaxed fellow, what are you complaining about? 

(Although, can you blame him? His name is one of the few which can be said while one is asleep, which thus imbibes him with a sense that, really, he need not actually do anything in life.....Maybe buy a horse and feed it? That might just about do it as a hobby.)
Wayne:
Option A: An ingrown toenail that’s red and swollen, painful to look at and even less fun to deal with when kicked. 

Option B: Of humble stock, his parents gave him that rather rural name in the hope he’d work hard and make something of himself. Did he? Well, you’d be surprised. Yes, many-a-Wayne slipped through the gaps and never got to rise up, but some Waynes used the force of their good heart to successfully propel themselves forward. 

(Note: The only real hiccup for both species is that they are hindered by the absence of the gene which enables a human to comprehend modern digital technology. Although, who knows? Perhaps it’s actually a blessing…)
Wayno: That line from the Bible should have read: "Bless those that carry a young heart like Wayno, for they are the ones to be emulated and they are the ones that will - and should - inherit the earth. Amen."
Wazza: Sweet-natured, reliable and irreverent, Wazza lives for embarking on adventures with his friends.
Webby: Never underestimate Webby. His simplicity is actually cohesion, not confusion.
Welchy: Welchy gets injured all the time and frowns whenever he’s in pain, which is quite a lot, unfortunately, but he is a fun-loving legend who lives his life in his jocks.
Wendell: (Ancestor of Bruce.) Back in the dark ages, in Europe, invading forces would attempt to bust open the gates of a castle with a giant log carried by twenty men or more, who would slam it repeatedly against them. In the absence of any smashing device, however, they’d just grab Wendell, pick him up side-on, and crunch his tremendously large and dense cranium against the gates, instead. It never really bothered Wendell because all he knew of it was a rather loud knocking noise.
Wentzel: A big, round South African beetle who pushes the other bugs out of the way in order to get to the pollen/sugar/dung heap first. And when he gets there he engorges himself to obesity with the expectation that this massive increase in body fat is will attract females for miles. (Wentzel, that’s great, but you should probably wipe your face before you embark on the hunt for a mate, mate.)
Wes: Wes is a big bloke. He knows how to fight a fire, he’s familiar with nearly every part of most old cars, he’s handy with a welder, he can defend himself, he makes people laugh and at the end of a long day, or even during an annual local festival, he loves a good, cold beer. Howdy Wes.
Wesley: The Wesley Treatment is what happens to anything – sandwiches and packs of soft drink cans, for example – when it is wrapped tightly in clear plastic film.
West: Yep, he's definitely out there, all right. Not the academic type, West is his own man who trusts his decisions and not for a moment would he heed advice from someone he didn't respect - unless it involved some perilous task, chore or adventure he didn't know much about. Women adore him, partly because of his looks, but mostly because he exudes an untameable, dangerous vibe. West.
Weston: Often wearing a high-viz shirt or jacket, Weston is a working man and a cheeky one. His needs are simple and his friendship is genuine, which is a common theme amid the working class.
Westy: Extremely difficult to take down, be it philosophically, physically or emotionally, Westy is one step ahead of the game. He rarely takes work stresses home with him. Hang on, hang on…actually, that's a good point. Does he work??
Weylin: Weylin hasn't dusted around his house since before his wife left him, and that was way back in the 60's, not long before he shot his horse through insanity. (His, not the horses.)
Whacky: (If only he was so lucky.) Whacky is intelligent and methodical.
Whitney: You'd hope that the only way a man is called Whitney is because his surname is Houston. In which case Whitney can barely wipe the smile from his face, no matter what he's doing. Indeed, the more he is called Whitney, the more fun he seems to have. And he isn't little.
Wilbur: The name of a woollen tea cosie that hippies put on their head at dance festivals.
Wilco: Not prone to flaunting it in public, Wilco is far more subversive and cool. He's the sort of bloke who is worth millions behind the scenes, but is actually more content in some simple life which contains the bare essentials. Rarely manic or in-your-face angry, he moves in line with things called gravity and momentum. As the Buddhists say, life should be like pouring water down hill, and this sums up Wilco nicely. (Yes, this might mean he is occasionally seen as lazy, such is life.)
Wilder:
One can envisage Wilder reclining on a Chesterfield sofa, smoking a Cuban with one hand and swirling a brandy with the other, trying to ignore some bullshit as spoken by an ill-informed idiot about peak oil and it's imminent, theoretical impact on Wilder's rather expansive share portfolio, which, by the way, he attained through guile, a natural desire to take the odd risk and a general belief that all money markets are just a game. 

Certainly, ain't nothing too crazy about Wilder, ladies and gentlemen, but he does tend to succeed.
Wilfred: Wilfred accepts the odd kick-back with a shrug of his shoulders. As the CEO of a large, successful company who has come to realise that life is something of a silly game, he's done his fair share of hard work and now understands life can't be taken too seriously. So, yes, he has had hookers under his desk performing deeds we can't talk about here while at the same time interviewing people in front of him. On the other hand, he's given millions away to charities who need help. Such is Wilfred.
Will: Will is almost too nice for his own good. He was a textbook student in his younger day and in adulthood he rushes to the aid of all and everyone. He makes an excellent grief counsellor, school teacher or ambulance driver.
Willem: Willem slides underneath the surface like a large and able Eagle Ray. He moves easily, stealthily, almost, and he doesn't really get involved with predictable life paths.
William: A sage who has seen and done it all; war, love, family, everything. Now that he’s an old man he likes to sit outside in the morning sun, where he reads the paper and quietly reminisces about his wonderful life that is coming to a close.
Willis: A good friend and possible work colleague of Solomon.
Wilson: Wilson opens his front door each morning on the way to work or where ever, and some tiny part of him always expects his minions to be there to greet him, frothing at how excited they are to behold his greatness. They're never there of course, but he likes the idea...
Winslow: Winslow is a big guy who is very hard to take down, either because of his actual physical size or his constant massive grin, and both are equally undeniable on a person. It helps that Winslow is almost certain to have a large chunk of islander DNA in him and once he starts laughing it infects the entire village. Nice work Winslow.
Winston:
Option A: Winston walks into the shed where his friend is working, careful not to cut himself on anything while he looks around curiously.
"What's this thing?" he asks, picking up a strange looking implement he's never seen before.
His friend looks at him and smiles. "Winston, it's a hammer, mate. We use them to hit these things called nails."
"Oh, yes," Winston says earnestly. "I know that. I mean, what I meant to say was, how long have you had it?"

Option B: An indigenous elder who has scars on his body and face from initiation ceremonies, many years ago. He talks to the dead and he even sees the future sometimes. You don't wanna do wrong by Winston and his kin for he might even point the bone, and if he does it will be well-deserved.
Winter: It's not snowing in your jocks is it, mate? No? Good, then smile and stop trying to look and act cool. Where’s the fun in that? Girls prefer a smile anyway.
Wiremu: Wiremu is either married to, or the brother of, a girl called Tuhi. Neither of them are particularly normal.
Wise: Unathletic. Wise lives on his game pad, his tablet or in front of his computer screen. Wise, some advise from management: you're a smart, funny indivudual so get outside and throw out thy evil devices! Use that body of yours before it's too late. Run. Jump. Get a skateboard and ride it down a freeway. Parachute. We don’t care, just do something. But most important, TRAVEL, AND TALK TO EVERYONE YOU MEET. That's where the real fun is.
Wojtek: Pronounced Voy-tek, he is his own man all right, in every situation. Uncompromising and reasonably unforgiving, Wojtek, don’t take this the wrong way, but can we suggest you lighten-the-fuck up? (His Eastern European heritage however means there might only be a small chance of that happening.)
Woodrow:
I think most of us in this room acknowledge Woodrow is never going to be the fastest member of the team, but that isn't his job. As a brilliant strategist, Woodrow looks likes he's barely moving, and this brings us to a salient point. His success isn't a fluke, and it can be put down to two things: 

1: He mysteriously knows where the ball is going to be in about 20 minutes time.

2: As a gifted lateral thinker with a calm persona, when the plan he's concocted doesn't come to fruition, he'll constantly adapt and plot without so much as a frown on his ample forehead, which means all those watching think that he's planned the whole thing anyway.
Woody: Woody is rock solid and another comic genius. He loves women and he loves his life.
Woolfy: Woolfy is that cheeky prick who itches for a bit of chaos.
Wylie: Ever seen that ad for Corona? I think it's set in Mexico. You know the one - three blonde, surf hippies are each sitting on a box of Corona stubbies, beer in hand, and they're looking out to a sunset-lit surf break where someone is carving it up. Wylie may or may not be the bloke on the wave, but he's definitely one of the dudes sitting on one of the Corona boxes, enjoying an ale, laughing with some gorgeous surf-girl, and contemplating dinner and a doobie afterwards. Wylie.
Wyllim: The prophylactic used by men of distinction.
Wyn:
And he does too, but never by using brute force or stand-over tactics. Wyn prevails by being dedicated and persistent, and by having a passion for what he does. As a matter of fact, if he’s really concentrating he’s almost unapproachable. Not out of rudeness you understand, but just because great devotion and attention to detail requires maximal attention. (And, predictably, he always builds a loving, tight family.) 
Nice one Wyn.
